notes:
ADVERSARIAL READ vs /images/blueprints/factory/99434c44259b__3420__Nylon.jpg.

WHAT THE DRAWING SPECIFIES: the trouser front with the fly laid OPEN. A red dotted line runs vertically down the centre of the fly (the zipper) and a second red dotted line follows the curved fly-facing edge. The waistband extension with its buttonhole sits at the top; belt loops and a front pleat are drawn on the left.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED:
(1) Metal zip instead of nylon coil — the only thing that separates this option from its siblings? No. The zip reads as a fine continuous matte spiral with no individual bright metal teeth and no metal sheen; it is a coil zip.
(2) Button fly substituted (the commonest tailoring prior for a bespoke trouser)? No — there is a zip, and it is open and visible.
(3) Fly closed, hiding the closure entirely? No — the fly is open exactly as drawn, which is the whole point of this blueprint.
(4) Exposed sport-zip styling? No — the zip sits behind the fly facing, concealed in the normal way when closed.
(5) Red traced from the drawing's dotted annotation lines? No — the zip and facing are tonal charcoal; no red, no dotted callouts, no numbers.
(6) Wrong face of the garment? No — trouser front with waistband, belt loop, pleat and fly, as drawn.

No critical or major findings.
